Honestly after goblin america's demo I was expecting a surreal departure from the concept at some point, even as a final gag. Freedom isn't free and a hard throw into a completely different type of game, or if gil was being lazy, maybe right into the goblin america demo with no warning or explanation. Or the weird skull nail that was poking fun at inscryption to kick off some absurdly pointless ARG that gives you some code to put into the game to unlock golden planks that do nothing but say "wishlist goblin america" on gold planks. Or a pivot to just an actual card game, but it's just poker with your husband before he leaves. I am excited for Goblin America. I clearly saw this was a joke to poke at trends in games with an extremely on the nose gag with some of the same surrealism in what we've seen of goblin america, and then I expected a punchline. It's possible I missed it, but in general I guess I just want jokes to be funny. If it was a dollar, I might feel more 50/50 on eh, but I guess I didn't really feel like I got 3 dollars worth of chuckle. I guess I didn't really get a dollars worth, either. The trailer gives you the whole joke, and there is nothing more beyond that. I wish there was. Now go wishlist goblin america

OK SO, Starts strong, makes the joke clear and fun. the nail changing into different things is fun and random... You will see everything the game has to offer in like 10 minutes. There is a nail that hints at something bigger but the shoe never drops. like, you can get 1 mil quick then the game ends. the achievements for fully upgrading a tool and Fully upgrading all tools are bugged and impossible to get currently. This game also has no soundtrack, no ambient noise beyond the light buzzing and blinking. there are sound effects for Husband talking and buying things but thats about it. Nothing deeper happens at any point. ALSO THESE AREN'T EVEN PLANKS YOU'D USE BUILD A DECK?! they are too thick and, on top of that, aren't laid in a way that properly covers the entire deck so its not even a properly built deck! The upgrades don't all reflect in game well either. Maxed out gold nail? After driving it into the plank it turns into the default. Maxed out planks? Still look old and worn even when laying it. why not change the wood to different textures to convey better wood? Tint it yellow for pine, a rich brown for oak, a deep red for mahogany. Maybe I am wrong and I don't get it, but I still can't recommend it

If you just want to have some fun for like, a half hour, then I say give it a shot. If you're looking for a game with real content, real mechanics, then I highly suggest going somewhere else. Every mechanic in this game is meant to be a detriment to you, the player. There is not a single mechanic in this game designed to be of benefit to you. There's only one nail that's truly and entirely beneficial to you. The glass nail is great once you get used to it, but you gotta figure it out. The bomb nail, as far as I can tell, is impossible to perfect so it's designed to entirely ruin your streak. Then you've got the bugs which seemingly only spawn underneath your hand or in the corners you've already nailed, so they're impossible to splat for money. Perfects are insanely inconsistent. I had more perfect streaks without any upgrades than I did after a couple hammer and glove upgrades. Not to mention the fact that every time you place the nail, your hammer goes one of two places and gets stuck until you wildly flail your mouse around. Either it gets stuck under the plank, or under the nail head. And inevitably in the massive flurry of swinging movements, you hit your hand at least once, if not multiple times, losing both money and any streak you might've had. Oh, there's also a speed running achievement in this game... A game designed to torture you and slow you down every step of the way... Yeah, it's a funny game for like 5 minutes, but boy did they miss in every other aspect of this game...

As far as gag games go, the title is brilliant. You build decks while a rogue light flickers. But really, that's about all there is to praise here. Rogue Light Deck Builder isn't meaningfully substantive or entertaining beyond the novelty of its own existence. The presentation of this hellish deck-building loop is quirky enough but that charm wears thin shortly and you're still left with the lackluster game loop. Rogue Light Deck Builder isn't so much meant to be played as described to your friends, that you may see them titter when they catch on to the punchline. And that's fine but I wouldn't recommend it as a game.
